title: Does steering toward 'honesty' actually increase calibration, or just verbosity of hedging?

original_idea.body: Build an honesty/uncertainty vector; measure ECE/calibration before and after steering on a ground-truth QA set to distinguish real calibration gain from blanket hedging.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Calibration-vs-hedging matters but indirect catastrophic-risk link; gap (level 3).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Honesty vector + ECE metrics on a QA set with one open model; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear success criterion (calibration curves before/after) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public model, cheap calibration eval, externally runnable (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Steering + inference + metrics, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Honesty steering and calibration studied; discrimination angle partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cosmetic-hedging-vs-calibration discrimination may be partly open.
